claims.title: Finite-cycle DAC theory,graded-liquid regeneration and failed routing

quoted_fields.interface: The producer constructs a finite-cycle electrochemical direct-air-capture model closing carbon,ions,water,charge,finite-cell Gibbs loss and periodic reset exchange/duty,with an explicit resistance-work relation and16-fraction periodic liquid regenerator. The full <=60kJ/mol delivered-CO2,all-installed-area sustained-throughput capability is NOT ACHIEVED:joint cold-electrode performance is unmeasured and the attempted low-inventory feed/return routing fails its final geometric audit. No hardware was fabricated.
quoted_fields.failure: The attempted manifold cases0.5/0.8/1.2/2.0L/m^2 per side have reported minimum surface clearances+17.27/-29.10/-87.89/-117.46micrometres versus required30micrometre solid wall;the latter three intersect,and terminal combs also cross opposite fingers without supplied layers/vias. These hydraulic-network calculations retain conditional value but their physical routing interpretation is rejected. This is failure of the attempted geometries,not a no-go for every routing design. A larger real manifold changes retained volume,reset exchange/downtime and current;pressure also changes water transport and reciprocal electrical work. Merely adding a pump-energy estimate does not close delivered performance. Proposed ionic/electronic/kinetic properties and modeled displacement response remain unmeasured together. Source comparator pilot energy/flux and separate long-duration smaller-device records stay separate;target flux is not demonstrated superiority. Mathematical/numerical consistency is not physical coefficient validation,practical compactness or historical priority.
